objectives: Decode taught pr-words by mapping graphemes in order.
Blend /p/ and /r/ smoothly before the vowel and ending.
Distinguish pram, press, print and prop by their remaining sounds.
Self-correct when a consonant or vowel is omitted.
concepts: The pr onset contains two phonemes, /p/ and /r/.
The vowel and ending distinguish words that share an onset.
Reading each grapheme in order supports accurate decoding.
Self-correction returns attention to the printed word.

definitions.definition: Use grapheme-to-phoneme knowledge to read a word.
A letter or letter group that represents a sound.
Notice a mismatch and reread the word accurately.

workedExamples.solution: Map p-r-e-ss and blend the sounds: press.
Both begin pr, but print has /i/ and ends /nt/, while prop has /o/ and ends /p/.

commonMistakes: Skipping /r/ and reading press without the blend.
Guessing from pr without reading the vowel and ending.
Confusing short vowels in pram, press and prop.
Reading only the onset instead of the complete word.
keyTakeaways: Decode the vowel and ending to identify the word.
Pram, press, print and prop have different rimes.
Reread the whole word to check every grapheme.

activities.name: Map and blend pr-words.
steps: Point to each grapheme from left to right.
Say /p/ then /r/ without an extra vowel.
Read the complete word and check it against the letters.

activities.name: Compare words with the same onset.
steps: Read pram, press, print and prop.
Identify the vowel and final sound group.
Explain how the endings distinguish the words.
Reread any word that does not match its letters.
